overview: This three-document file records correspondence between the U.S. Department of State’s Telecommunications Division and the Federal Communications Commission concerning SCAP’s proposal to revise telegraph-message rates between occupied Japan and the United States. The State Department sought the FCC’s views in February 1947; the FCC acknowledged the request while its broader investigation of overseas communications charges was pending, and in August reported that U.S. carriers had adopted increased “Bermuda” pattern rates of 30 cents per full-rate word and 20 cents per CDE word for traffic from the United States to Japan, suggesting negotiations over applying the same pattern and settlement arrangements in both directions.

subfiles.title: State Department request for FCC views on SCAP telegraph-rate proposal
subfiles.from: Francis Colt de Wolf, Chief, Telecommunications Division, Department of State
subfiles.to: William J. Norfleet, Chief Accountant, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.about: The State Department asks the FCC to assess a SCAP proposal to change telegraphic-message rates between Japan and the United States.
subfiles.summary: De Wolf forwards for the FCC’s consideration a copy of a February 13, 1947 communication from General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo. He requests the Commission’s views so that the Department can reply to SCAP. The listed enclosure itself is not present as a separate page in this file.

subfiles.title: FCC acknowledgment of the State Department’s rate inquiry
subfiles.from: T. J. Slowie, Secretary, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Francis Colt de Wolf, Chief, Telecommunications Division, Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC acknowledges the State Department’s inquiry and promises to place SCAP’s proposed telegraph-rate change before the Commission.
subfiles.summary: The FCC confirms receipt of de Wolf’s February 21 letter addressed to William J. Norfleet. Secretary T. J. Slowie states that the matter will be brought to the Commission’s attention at an early date and that the Department will be advised of the result.

subfiles.title: FCC decision on United States–Japan telegraph rates
subfiles.from: T. J. Slowie, Secretary, Federal Communications Commission
subfiles.to: Francis Colt de Wolf, Chief, Telecommunications Division, Department of State
subfiles.about: The FCC reports newly filed U.S.-to-Japan telegraph rates based on the “Bermuda” pattern and suggests discussing reciprocal arrangements with U.S. carriers.
subfiles.summary: Slowie explains that action on SCAP’s request had been deferred pending the FCC’s wider investigation of charges for communications between the United States and overseas and foreign points. Following the Commission’s decision, U.S. telegraph carriers filed “Bermuda” pattern rates from all parts of the United States to all parts of Japan: 30 cents per full-rate word and 20 cents per CDE word. The FCC suggests that SCAP discuss with the carriers whether this rate and settlement pattern should apply in both directions between Japan and the United States.

interest: The file provides a compact record of how occupation authorities, the State Department, the FCC, and private U.S. telegraph carriers interacted in setting postwar communications prices. Its chief evidentiary value is the August letter’s precise per-word rates and its reference to the “Bermuda” pattern as a possible bilateral framework for both rates and settlements. It also documents the relationship between a Japan-specific SCAP request and the FCC’s broader review of American overseas communications charges, while revealing that the enclosed February 13 SCAP communication and a referenced March 17 FCC letter are absent from this surviving bundle.
